scope: Build and verify MTH 215 completely before starting the detailed plan for PHS 104A. The existing shared app remains the foundation; other course outlines stay planned.

buildOrder.title: Course contracts and coverage register
buildOrder.work: Add typed released-course, module, objective, lesson-block, item-family, resource, and review records. Preserve these planning specifications separately from consumable lesson content. Create stable objective IDs matching the forty lesson IDs.
buildOrder.verification: Reject missing objectives, dangling prerequisites, duplicate IDs, invalid resource references, and unsupported lesson block types. All forty objectives appear in a coverage report with initially unbuilt status.

buildOrder.title: Lesson reader and accessible math
buildOrder.work: Add a course overview, module list, lesson route, previous/next links, resume action, expandable hints, answer inputs, a scratch-notes area, and readable mathematics. Display readiness, availability, and completion separately.
buildOrder.verification: Keyboard-only navigation, focus restoration after feedback, mathematical reading order, zoom, mobile layout, direct deep links, and a missing-lesson state work with one reviewed fixture lesson.

buildOrder.title: Attempt state and backup migration
buildOrder.work: Extend browser-local progress with versioned objective evidence and attempt records. Preserve v1 notes, queue, sessions, bookmarks, and preferences. Store concrete assessment instances before display; distinguish active, submitted, abandoned, and assisted attempts.
buildOrder.verification: Test v1-to-v2 migration, save/reload during an attempt, export/import round trips, malformed or future-version backups, size/quota failures, cross-tab conflicts, reset cancellation, and preservation of the prior valid save on failure.

buildOrder.title: Answer formats and deterministic generation
buildOrder.work: Implement bounded mathematical input and reviewed graders for exact/approximate numbers, choices, intervals, finite sets, supported expressions, matrices, and structured periodic answers. Introduce seeded families and immutable attempt snapshots.
buildOrder.verification: Use independently calculated fixtures for accepted equivalents, near misses, domain mismatches, malformed input, empty sets, repeated roots, poles, and singular matrices. Run bounded seed sweeps and verify generator failure behavior.

buildOrder.title: Foundation bridges and algebra lessons
buildOrder.work: Author b01 through b06 and all lessons in m01 and m02, including original examples, error feedback, practice, and checkpoints. Build equation-step, interval, function-table, and calibration activities.
buildOrder.verification: A learner can enter from a foundation gap, study the assigned bridge, complete an original lesson, receive correct feedback, save progress, and resume on a fresh visit.

buildOrder.title: Polynomial and rational lessons
buildOrder.work: Complete m03 and m04. Extend graphing to exact roots, multiplicity, holes, asymptotes, open/closed boundaries, sign charts, and restricted inverses.
buildOrder.verification: Check every graph against algebraic fixtures and table values. Ensure no line crosses an excluded discontinuity and all nonvisual alternatives convey the same assessed information.

buildOrder.title: Exponential and logarithmic lessons
buildOrder.work: Complete m05, including growth tables, domain-aware logarithm steps, parameter fitting, and threshold activities. Label all units and permitted approximations.
buildOrder.verification: Reject nonpositive log arguments and unreachable threshold cases. Verify exact and rounded answers independently and confirm the explanation matches the generated parameters.

buildOrder.title: Trigonometry lessons and tools
buildOrder.work: Complete m06, m07, and m08 in separate module-sized increments. Build the unit circle, periodic graph explorer, inverse-range comparison, identity-step review, complete-root list, and triangle solver activities.
buildOrder.verification: Exercise degree/radian modes, axis angles, negative angles, poles, equivalent phases, principal ranges, missing roots, interval endpoints, and ambiguous triangles. Every activity works with numeric and keyboard inputs.

buildOrder.title: Systems and matrix lessons
buildOrder.work: Complete m09 and m10, including equation-system comparison, matrix entry, operation compatibility, row reduction with undo, inverse checks, and residual comparisons.
buildOrder.verification: Verify unique, inconsistent, and dependent systems; rectangular dimensions; noncommutativity; zero pivots; singular inverses; exact fractions; and rounded residual examples.

buildOrder.title: Diagnostics, quizzes, and targeted review
buildOrder.work: Connect the foundation screen, course survey, module challenges, ten quizzes, custom practice, final blueprint, objective evidence, and due-review queue. Implement clear scope and assistance labels.
buildOrder.verification: Run full and refresher journeys. Confirm a survey alone cannot grant completion, a high total cannot hide an unassessed objective, and reloads do not change a running assessment's questions.

buildOrder.title: Measurement project and completion report
buildOrder.work: Build the six-part project notebook, structured checks, transparent rubric, revisions, report export, and completion summary. Separate self-review from independent review.
buildOrder.verification: Complete the reference project and at least two reviewed variants. Verify every required check, save/restore, rubric calculation, invalid submission, and project revision path.

buildOrder.title: Course audit and release review
buildOrder.work: Audit every objective and subtopic, review explanations and generator families, run accessibility and persistence checks, collect pilot feedback, resolve material defects, and report the pack's actual review status.
buildOrder.verification: Pass the release gates below. Only then begin PHS 104A planning; carry reusable components and lessons learned into that separate course plan.

interactionInventory.name: Equation and identity steps
interactionInventory.contract: Choose or enter a bounded next step, name its justification, preserve domain restrictions, undo, and compare equivalent statements.

interactionInventory.name: Number lines and sign charts
interactionInventory.contract: Set endpoints and inclusion with forms, classify signs on intervals, and show an equivalent readable interval list.

interactionInventory.name: Function and model explorer
interactionInventory.contract: Predict, change parameters with numeric/keyboard controls, inspect labeled graphs and tables, compare original and reduced forms, and reset to the same initial state.

interactionInventory.name: Unit circle and triangle explorer
interactionInventory.contract: Enter angles and sides with explicit units, show exact values when available, expose coordinate and ratio tables, and identify undefined or ambiguous cases.

interactionInventory.name: Periodic signal explorer
interactionInventory.contract: Control amplitude, offset, frequency, and phase; compare table values and complete solution sets; split the plot at poles and provide reduced-motion behavior.

interactionInventory.name: Systems and matrix workspace
interactionInventory.contract: Use labeled cells and variable order, show row-operation history, allow undo, compare equations and matrices, and check a candidate by residuals.

dataContract.content: A released pack references reviewed original lesson blocks and item families by immutable ID/version. Planning JSON must never be mistaken for complete lessons by the catalog.
dataContract.objectiveEvidence: Record objective ID, content version, attempt ID, independent/assisted status, score, validity checks, demonstratedAt, lastReviewedAt, and nextReviewAt. Keep self-reported familiarity separate.
dataContract.attempt: Record attempt ID, mode, status, course/blueprint version, generator version, seed, exact item snapshots, responses, submission time, assistance, and score details. Restarting practice creates a new attempt; resuming preserves the existing one.
dataContract.storage: Begin with a versioned extension of the existing local progress store. Measure a full-course history against its current 1 MB backup budget before release. Surface a capacity message with export and selective history-removal controls; do not silently discard notes or completed evidence. Any changed storage budget or storage backend must retain validated backup migration.
dataContract.concurrency: Detect that another tab changed the current attempt before overwriting it. Preserve the current answer draft and offer reload or keep-as-new-attempt; do not silently overwrite a submitted attempt.
dataContract.upgrades: Display when evidence belongs to an older content version. Preserve it, identify materially changed objectives, and suggest the relevant new check rather than resetting the whole course.
dataContract.privacy: Use generic public examples and local learner data. No transcript, personal grade, account creation, hosted execution service, or paid resource is required for MTH 215.

releaseGates.name: Coverage
releaseGates.requirement: All forty objectives and every listed required subtopic have a reviewed lesson, two worked examples, guided practice, an interaction, at least two distinct families, a checkpoint, a quiz mapping, and a final mapping. Six bridge routes and all six project tasks are usable.

releaseGates.name: Mathematical correctness
releaseGates.requirement: Review every explanation, anchor answer, identity step, domain restriction, unit, and rounding rule. All family seed sweeps and explicit edge fixtures pass. No unresolved error can misgrade valid work or teach an invalid rule.

releaseGates.name: Assessment integrity
releaseGates.requirement: Every formal form satisfies its objective/category distribution. Assisted practice cannot masquerade as independent success. Complete solution sets, critical validity repairs, and threshold calculations are tested. Item pools must contain enough eligible forms without silent duplication.

releaseGates.name: Accessible interaction
releaseGates.requirement: All course flows work with keyboard-only controls, visible focus, screen-reader labels, accessible math, 200 percent zoom, narrow mobile screens, and reduced motion. Graphs have equivalent text or tables. Automated checks supplement manual inspection.

releaseGates.name: Progress durability
releaseGates.requirement: Full and refresh journeys survive reload, import/export, version migration, invalid storage, quota exhaustion, and concurrent tabs. A storage failure is visible and cannot silently report a saved result.

releaseGates.name: Resources and publication
releaseGates.requirement: Reading references resolve to the intended provider and section. Original content attribution and external links are accurate. Availability indicators match implemented content. The build, lint, relevant unit checks, and browser journeys pass on the pushed branch.

releaseGates.name: Review status
releaseGates.requirement: Record authoring and verification results separately from an independent subject review and pilot feedback. The pack may be labeled preview when technically complete; label it reviewed only after that independent review and material feedback are resolved.

commitPolicy: Verify each small related slice, stage only its files, use a brief lowercase summary without a body or attribution trailers, commit, and immediately push origin/main. Do not include Markdown or personal records.
nextCourseNote: Follow the selected development order. Its future learner guidance must retain NU's published PHS 104 or PHS 171 prerequisite and distinguish laboratory simulations from any official kit or enrollment requirements.
